thread:
alice-cs: FYI customer (AcmeCorp) opened a ticket — their streaming TTFT / tokens/sec chart on the Console shows negative dips and a weird inversion for ~4h. They attached a screenshot and a couple request_ids. ticket# INC-4892 :frowning_face:

maya-support: Thanks. Can you paste the request_ids and the workspace/org? I'll try to reproduce quickly.

alice-cs: workspace acme-prod, route /v1/stream/generate, request_ids: r_20260317_aa12, r_20260317_bb34. Screenshot: shows tokens/sec at -1200 for a period, then spikes to +8000.

kevin-eng-metrics: hmm negative tokens/sec usually means negative delta between consecutive cumulative token counters. Two common culprits: out-of-order ingestion or clock skew on the aggregation host. Any recent deploys to the streaming-agg service?

rachel-prod-analytics: I just pulled the raw events for those request_ids from our metrics store. snippet:```json
{"req_id":"r_20260317_aa12","cum_tokens":1500,"ts":1700123450}
{"req_id":"r_20260317_aa12","cum_tokens":1300,"ts":1700123500}
```That shows cum_tokens decreasing -> negative delta.

maya-support: Customer says they didn't retry the client. They ran a single streaming request.

kevin-eng-metrics: Can you check consumer lag on the kafka topic metrics-streaming? If consumers lag and then get out-of-order segments from producers, we could see sequence issues. Also check if the ingest pipeline applies monotonic checks.

sre-bot: alert: kafka_consumer_group_lag(metrics-consumer): spike from 20->45k msgs between 1700123200-1700123800.

rachel-prod-analytics: Confirmed: consumer group lag spike around that window. Also noticed one aggregator pod (stream-agg-3) was restarted at 1700123333 (kubelet drain during node reprovision). That pod had older wallclock time by ~40s compared to others (ntp drift).

kevin-eng-metrics: That fits: aggregator restart + clock skew + reordering during backfill can yield negative deltas. Short term mitigation: clamp negative deltas to 0 in the UI/rollup (so graph doesn't go below zero) and flag those intervals as "out-of-order". Long term: make the aggregator compute delta using monotonic sequence numbers rather than wallclock timestamps, and drop/merge out-of-order updates.

maya-support: I'll propose the UI clamp + annotation to the customer as a mitigation. Customer wants an ETA for a fix, they flagged as P2.

alice-cs: What's the repro steps so we can tell customer how we investigated?

kevin-eng-metrics: Repro steps I used: 1) query raw metrics:```select * from streaming_metrics_raw where req_id in ('r_20260317_aa12','r_20260317_bb34') order by ts;```2) observe cum_tokens decreasing between consecutive rows -> negative delta. 3) check kafka lag:```kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka.internal:9092 --describe --group metrics-consumer``` and note lag spike. 4) check k8s events for stream-agg pods:```kubectl get pods -n infra | grep stream-agg``` and look at pod restart times. 5) check ntp/drift on node:```timedatectl status```

rachel-prod-analytics: I also ran a quick script to detect negative deltas across last 24h:```python
# quick check
rows = sql("select req_id,ts,cum_tokens from streaming_metrics_raw where ts >= now() - interval '24 hours'")
for r in rows:
  # compare with previous per req_id
  ...
# found ~112 negative-delta intervals, concentrated around 1700123000-1700123900
```

sre-bot: note: node ip 10.12.5.7 had ntp offset ~-42s during that window.

kevin-eng-metrics: Action items: (1) maya/support to tell AcmeCorp the root cause appears to be aggregator restart + ntp drift + kafka consumer lag leading to out-of-order ingestion; mitigation is clamping/annotation in UI. (2) eng-metrics to add server-side monotonic sequence check and drop negative deltas before writing rollups. (3) eng-sre to put in place ntp/chrony alert for >5s offset and fix drift on infra nodes. (4) product to add visual flag for "data backfill / corrected" intervals in Console.

maya-support: I'll communicate the mitigation and P2 ETA ~48-72h. I'll also ask customer if they can share a short timeline of their request to help cross-check logs.

alice-cs: kevin, can you post a quick patch suggestion for the UI clamp so we can push to prod as interim?

kevin-eng-metrics: Quick UI change: in streaming chart renderer, replace value = raw_delta with value = max(0, raw_delta) and add meta: "note":"some intervals had out-of-order events; values clamped". PR draft: `redwood/console#fix/streaming-clamp-1792`

rachel-prod-analytics: I'll schedule a follow-up to re-run the negative-delta detector after the consumer group stabilizes.

sre-bot: jira: SRE-317 created for ntp drift monitor. eng-metrics ticket EM-642 created for monotonic seq enforcement.

alice-cs: thanks all. maya, please paste customer's reply when you get it. I'll keep INC-4892 updated. :thumbsup:
